chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:

There is no servant who withholds any part of the zakat of his wealth except that Allah will make it, on the Day of Resurrection, a serpent of fire encircled around his neck, biting from his flesh until the reckoning is finished.
And this is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"They will be encircled by what they were miserly with on the Day of Resurrection."
Meaning what they were miserly with from the zakat.

key_terms.الْحِسَابِ: the reckoning or accounting of deeds
key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are raised and judged
key_terms.بَخِلُوا: they were miserly and withheld what was due
key_terms.ثُعْبَانًا: a serpent, here describing a form of punishment
key_terms.زَكَاةِ: zakat, the obligatory alms due from wealth
key_terms.مُطَوَّقًا: encircled or fastened around the neck

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who withholds zakat according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith warns that withholding zakat has severe consequences in the afterlife, where the withheld wealth becomes a torment for its owner on the Day of Resurrection. It also explains the Qur'anic verse as referring specifically to miserliness in paying zakat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1587 - Muhammad ibn Muslim reported from Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) who said:

"There is no servant who withholds any part of the Zakat of his wealth except that Allah (swt) will turn it on the Day of Resurrection into a snake of fire, coiled around his neck, biting into his flesh until the reckoning is complete.
This is the meaning of Allah’s (swt) statement:
'They will be encircled by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection' (Surah Ali ‘Imran 3:180),
referring to what they withheld from Zakat."
